thread:
maria: RFC follow-up — compact-seed bundles + tombstone markers for air-gapped upgrades. Quick question about operator dry-run semantics: should dry-run simulate tombstone effects (report-only) or also validate availability of delete targets? pinging arch/eng-runtime for tradeoffs.

samir: i'd vote report-only for dry-run. Dry-run should show a list of 'would-remove' blobs and staged activation steps, but not mutate any local caches. That keeps accidental deletes impossible. :thumbsup:

jia: agree on report-only. couple of followups: 1) we need deterministic apply ordering in manifest so dry-run can exactly mirror a real run, 2) we need an explicit activation marker so rollback is clear. sketch: 

```
manifest:
  format: compact-seed-v1
  epoch: 2026-03-15
  seq: 42
  blobs:
    - id: sha256:abc123
      size: 120MB
    - id: sha256:def456
      size: 80MB
  tombstones:
    - id: sha256:deadbeef
  apply_plan:
    - step: fetch
      target: sha256:abc123
    - step: stage
      target: sha256:abc123
    - step: activate
      marker: activation-42
```

If dry-run prints the apply_plan + tombstones -> operator can inspect and decide.

maria: good. what about partial-apply and resume when network drops? airgap gateways often flake mid-transfer. we need resume semantics that tie to manifest seq and activation marker.

samir: resume should be blob-level idempotent. fetchers must support range resume and a content-addressed temp path (e.g., /var/lib/redwood/tmp/sha256:...-inflight). on reconnection, continue until blob complete. activation only flips marker when all fetch+stage steps are done.

jia: +1. also think about tombstone semantics during resume: if a manifest references a tombstone for a blob that isn't present locally (or partially fetched) treat it as no-op for apply; still report it in dry-run. if a tombstone references a blob present in store, delete only after activation window passes or operator confirms. we should not delete during streaming apply.

ops-bot: deploy-check: compact-seed-v1 manifest schema validated by schema-checker v0.9 — OK. CI note: add test for tombstone reporting in dry-run.

maria: UX question for operators: should we add `--apply --review-only` mode (two-step) vs `--apply --autoconfirm`? i prefer explicit two-step: review -> apply.

todd: two-step is safer. also propose a `--shadow-apply` that stages blobs under a different activation marker (shadow-<seq>) so you can smoke-test with the new files without flipping production marker. then `promote shadow-<seq>` flips marker once tests pass.

samir: shadow-apply seems useful for customers that want canaries in place without separate clusters. implementation: stage into /data/activation-shadow-<seq>/ then symlink swap at activation. must ensure KV cache and model runtime pick up new path atomically.

jia: runtime concern: swapping symlink atomically is platform-dependent for some orchestration. consider activation that writes an activation metadata file and the runtime watches that file and performs an atomic rename on its internal pointer (not relying on fs symlink semantics). this avoids races with running processes.

maria: good call. last thing — offline seed distribution (USB/airgap shuttle) variant: manifest should support "seed-only" bundles that contain indexes + small deltas but not all blobs. operator must be warned if missing blobs exist; dry-run should include a manifest status: MISSING_BLOBS list so operator can reconcile via a seed shuttle.

samir: yep. also add a tombstone-ttl field: if tombstone has ttl > 0, deletion is deferred until TTL expires after activation sequence. That buys a safety window to re-seed if we accidentally tombstoned something important.

jia: edge-case: two manifests with same seq from different sources — need a canonical signer identity + signed epoch chain. accept manifest only if it chains with previous activation marker signed by the same operator key or by delegated signer. otherwise reject. include signer: who field in manifest.

maria: agreed. I'll update the RFC with these points: 
- dry-run = report-only (would-fetch, would-remove)
- deterministic apply_plan in manifest
- activation marker + shadow-apply flow
- resume: blob-level idempotent temp paths
- tombstone semantic: report-only until activation + optional ttl
- seed-only bundles and MISSING_BLOBS reporting
- manifest signer chaining requirement

maria: tagging implementers @samir @jia @todd — can you review the draft changes in the RFC PR? i'll add unit tests for schema and a dry-run integration test.

samir: will review today.

jia: on it, will add runtime watcher proposal.

todd: will sketch promote/shadow UX and a small operator CLI flow.

ops-bot: reminder: RFC PR #487 needs to include changelog entry and migration notes. :bell:

maria: thanks all. landing plan: iterate over PR, schedule a 30m sync next Tue for activation swapping constraints. :calendar:
